target_customer: Mobile freemium game developers seeking funding or publishing, and the investors and publishers who scout them
problem: Mobile game developers could not tell how their game compared with top grossing peers or find funding, while investors and publishers had no screened way to find promising games.
business_model: Free scouting reports and game profile pages as a funnel to game-backed loans and an ad-install data co-op
product_category: Mobile games analytics and funding marketplace

founders.name: Tim Ogilvie
founders.background_notes: Named as founder by TechCrunch (2014-03-20) and the YC page.

founders.name: Ted Shergalis
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by TechCrunch (2014-03-20); not listed on the YC page.

founders.name: Michael Hoydich
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder; TechCrunch calls him co-founder and founder of Squrl.

competitors.name: App Annie (with Distimo)
competitors.what: Mobile app store analytics and market data, including games revenue and rankings
competitors.traction_then: Acquired rival Distimo in May 2014, combining the two largest app analytics datasets
competitors.funding_then: Closed a $17 million round alongside the Distimo deal

technical_complexity.rationale: Scraping and modelling public chart data for 5000+ games was standard data work for a very small team, though the proprietary dataset and scoring model took some effort.

defensibility.rationale: The dataset of analyzed games and the ad co-op data could accrue over time, but large analytics vendors already held broader data and the scoring was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: App Annie absorbed Distimo in May 2014 and covered games analytics broadly; no source shows any incumbent acting on Think Gaming specifically.

market_need_then: Mobile games was a fast growing freemium market in 2014 and developers needed benchmarks and user acquisition funding; TechCrunch in March 2014 described profile pages meant to help developers find investors, acquirers and partners.

branding.domain_note: Used thinkgaming.com; the site returned HTTP 503 when fetched.

identity.voice_and_tone: Data science framing: free Scouting Reports that score a game's chance of becoming a top grosser.

branding.brand_signature: Scouting Reports that score mobile games

brand_strength.rationale: Generic descriptive name; press covered the product (Scouting Reports, ad co-op) but no source shows brand-level recognition.

pivots.from: Scouting reports and game profile pages for investors (TechCrunch 2014-03-20)
pivots.to: Mobile advertising co-op that shares install cost data across 400+ publishers and ad networks (TechCrunch 2014-07-29)
pivots.why: Not stated in the sources opened; seen as a product extension in the 2014-07-29 TechCrunch headline.

outcome_analysis: Think Gaming launched scouting reports and profile pages in early 2014, joined YC in summer 2014 with a team of one on the YC page, and added an ad install co-op that July. Only a small seed round of about 120 thousand dollars is reported. Aggregators list the company as dead but no post-mortem, acquisition or shutdown announcement was found, so the cause of failure is not public and no failure factors are assigned.
notes: Funding conflicts: Xconomy headline reports a 120,000 dollar seed (2014-08-19), Dealroom lists 125k, CB Insights lists 20K on 2014-08-20; the Xconomy page could not be opened (HTTP 503) so the figure rests on the headline seen in search results and the round rests on a single outlet plus databases. Investors beyond YC are unknown. Latka and CB Insights mark the company dead; Latka's 2021 revenue figure is unverified. Company site returned HTTP 503. Name origin not found.
